english.title: Fail to notify the deactivation / destruction / loss of a shotgun
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the holder of a

(A)_[certificate]_
(B)_[visitor's permit]_

relating to a shotgun, namely **(..SPECIFY SHOTGUN..), which had been

(C)_[deactivated,]_
(D)_[destroyed,]_
(E)_[lost,]_

failed, without reasonable excuse, to comply with section 34(1) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1997 in that you did not, within seven days of that event, give notice of it, by registered post or recorded delivery service, to the Chief Officer of Police for **(..SPECIFY THE POLICE FORCE..) who had granted your

(F)_[certificate.]_
(G)_[permit.]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 34(4) and 36(b) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1997.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 34(5) for the meaning of "deactivated".
(ii) See also associated offence wording H1277 re failure to give proper notice of deactivation/destruction/loss of shotgun.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
48 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
